write_up: A recruiter sees a progression from line cook to kitchen manager, with current responsibility for a 180-seat restaurant. The hesitation comes next: the schedule, ordering, inspections and training are all named, but the details of how you handle them are mostly missing.

The 180-seat line is the model. It names the job and gives the recruiter something concrete to hold. Add the size of the team and a few specifics about ordering, inspections and training to make the rest as useful.

cards.line: - Run the kitchen for a 180-seat restaurant
cards.cannot_tell: This gives the kitchen manager job a setting and a size in one short line. Use it as a model for the bullets below.

cards.line: - Manage the kitchen staff schedule
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell how many people you schedule or what the schedule has to cover. That's useful context for a kitchen manager job.
cards.example: Manage the kitchen staff schedule for [number] staff, covering [shifts or scheduling needs]
cards.question: How many staff do you schedule, and what shifts or scheduling needs do you cover?

cards.line: - Order food and supplies from vendors
cards.cannot_tell: Ordering is part of the job, but this doesn't show how you decide what or when to order. A detail about the process would make the responsibility more concrete.
cards.example: Order food and supplies from vendors using [ordering process] to meet [kitchen needs]
cards.question: How do you decide what to order, and what kitchen needs are you planning for?

cards.line: - Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections
cards.cannot_tell: This names an important responsibility, but not the checks or practices you use to keep the kitchen ready.
cards.example: Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections by [specific checks or practices]
cards.question: What checks or practices do you use to prepare the kitchen for health inspections?

cards.line: - Train new line cooks
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what you teach new cooks or how you train them.
cards.example: Train new line cooks on [skills or stations] through [training approach]
cards.question: What do you train new line cooks to do, and how do you train them?

cards.line: - Ran the line on busy weekend shifts
cards.cannot_tell: Running the line says what you owned, but not what the shift involved. Give the recruiter one detail about the work.
cards.example: Ran the line on busy weekend shifts, coordinating [people or tasks] during [service details]
cards.question: What did you coordinate when running the line on weekend shifts?

cards.line: - Helped plan seasonal menu changes
cards.cannot_tell: Helped keeps your ownership honest, but it leaves your contribution open. What part of the planning was yours?
cards.example: Helped plan seasonal menu changes by [your contribution]
cards.question: What did you contribute to planning the seasonal menu changes?

fit.note: Your experience points toward kitchen management and sous chef work. The progression and ServSafe Manager certification are easy to find; the team and management details would strengthen the case for your current level.
